title: Hotel Floor
intro: This is the one for the road. You don't need any kit. One yoga mat of floor and twelve minutes is enough. Four positions, held long, and you breathe through each one. They're where tennis and padel players tend to feel tight: the front of the hip, the groin, the turn through the hips, and the overhead side. Pad your knees with a towel or a folded shirt. A stretch should feel like a firm pull that fades as you breathe out, never a sharp or burning one.

Holding a stretch tonight won't make you flexible tomorrow, that comes from doing it again and again over weeks. What you get is feeling looser and a calm way to end the day. If you want real range at the hip and groin, do Wide Ball in the Mobility list. Don't do the long holds before you play, because they dull your power for a while.

before.label: Stop and get it looked at
before.text: Sharp pain, pins and needles, or anything running down a leg or an arm isn't a stretch, so stop that one.

before.label: Leave out
before.text: If a groin or a hamstring is still sore from playing, leave the wide and deep ones out.

before.label: Swollen calf
before.text: If one calf is swollen, warm or tender and you didn't strain it playing, see a doctor the same day.

good: On hands and knees, slowly round your back up then let it sink, staying in the middle of the range
Feel your whole spine moving a little at a time
bad: Pushing to the end of the range on either side

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach

good: Squeeze the back glute, then reach the arm on the same side as your back knee overhead
Feel it at the front of the back hip
bad: Arching your lower back to feel more

exercises.name: Frog Stretch
exercises.note: If a groin is sore now or grabbed on you lately, skip this one.

good: On hands and knees, slide your knees wide and sink your hips back toward your heels
Feel the inside of your thighs lengthen, a firm pull that fades as you breathe out
bad: Forcing your knees wider than feels comfortable

good: Sit on a folded towel with both knees bent at ninety degrees, then fold your chest over the front shin only as far as your back stays long
Feel it deep in the back hip of the front leg
bad: Forcing it when you feel a twinge in the knee instead of the hip

good: From hands and knees, walk your hands forward and let your chest sink toward the floor
Feel the stretch through your armpits and upper back
bad: Forcing your chest down if your shoulder pinches
